newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU rejects Dutch farm price text, awaits revisions.
newsitem.headline: EU rejects Dutch farm price text, awaits revisions.

text.p: European Union farm ministers on Tuesday rejected a compromise 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package and asked the Dutch EU Presidency to prepare a new one, a Dutch spokesman said.
Ministers opposed a proposal to slash payments to cereals farmers in order to help fund aid to beef producers hit by a fall in prices due to the mad cow crisis.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler also rejected the compromise because it included a demand for cereals set-aside to be fixed at an unchanged five percent in 1998/99.
The spokesman said that after further bilateral discussions on Tuesday evening the Dutch Farm Minister Jozias Van Aartses will present a new compromise text early on Wednesday.
"In past years the first compromise has never been the final one and at least two have been needed," the spokesman said. "We shall try to get an agreement during civilised working hours."
The annual EU farm price package has traditionally been agreed only after at least one all-night negotiating session.
